posts.name: Julis James
posts.cooked:
I’m looking for an experienced n8n automation expert to help design and build a reliable lead management workflow. This is a paid opportunity for someone who can understand the requirements, recommend the right approach, and deliver a working solution.

The workflow should cover three main areas:

1. Lead Collection and Qualification

I need to collect leads from forms and other sources, validate their information, identify duplicates, and use AI to categorize them based on their needs and suitability. Incomplete submissions should be flagged for review rather than processed blindly.

2. Data Synchronization and Follow Ups

Qualified leads should be stored in a central database or CRM, with relevant team notifications and automated follow ups. The workflow must keep records consistent and avoid duplicate messages or unnecessary follow ups.

3. Error Handling and Reliability

The workflow should handle API failures, rate limits, and incomplete executions properly. It should retry recoverable errors, prevent duplicate actions when an execution resumes, and make failed leads easy to identify and review.

I’m looking for someone who can build this properly, explain the technical decisions, and ensure the workflow is maintainable after delivery.

If you’re an experienced n8n developer interested in taking on this paid project, please comment with your relevant experience, how you would approach the build, and an estimate of the information you’d need to provide a quote.

Hi @Manisman , a reliable way to structure this would be to separate the workflow into three connected stages: lead intake, lead management, and execution monitoring.

For lead intake, incoming data from different sources should pass through a common validation process. This includes checking required fields, normalizing email addresses and phone numbers, identifying existing contacts, and using AI to categorize leads against defined qualification criteria. Incomplete or uncertain submissions should be routed for human review.

For lead management, every lead should have a consistent record containing its source, qualification status, assigned team member, and follow-up history. This makes CRM updates, team notifications, and follow-up scheduling easier to coordinate. It also helps prevent duplicate records and messages to leads who have already responded.

For execution monitoring, error handling should account for API failures, rate limits, and interrupted executions. Each stage should record its outcome so failed operations can be retried without repeating actions that have already succeeded.

For full disclosure, I’m affiliated with Pond AI, where custom AI agents and automation workflows are built and maintained. Pond AI can provide a free workflow architecture map that you can keep and implement yourself or hand to another developer. If you choose to have Pond AI handle the build, there’s a 7 day refund policy.

How many lead sources are you planning to connect, and do they all need to feed into the same CRM or database?

Hi Manisman,

I’m interested in your lead management automation project.

I have hands-on experience building n8n workflows, including an AI Lead Qualification & Follow-up system using Google Sheets, AI, email, and Telegram.

My previous project includes:

  • Lead collection and data validation.

  • Duplicate lead detection.

  • AI-based lead scoring (HOT, WARM, COLD).

  • Automated email follow-ups.

  • Telegram notifications.

For your project, I would approach it in stages:

  1. Lead collection and validation.

  2. Duplicate detection and AI qualification.

  3. Data synchronization with your CRM or database.

  4. Automated follow-ups and team notifications.

  5. Error handling, retry logic, and workflow testing.

To provide an accurate quote, I’d like to understand:

  • What are your lead sources?

  • Which CRM or database do you prefer?

  • Which AI provider and follow-up channels do you use?

  • Approximately how many leads do you process daily?

I’d be happy to discuss the requirements and share a demonstration of my previous work.

Best regards,
Nurul

posts.name: Julis James
posts.cooked:
Thanks for this breakdown. The three-stage structure is close to what I’m looking for. The intention is to bring leads from multiple sources into one central system, rather than maintain separate lead management processes for each source.

I’m particularly interested in making sure the validation and duplicate checks happen before qualification, so the same contact isn’t processed multiple times.

Hello @Manisman , another important factor is ensuring the workflow remains manageable as lead volume increases and more applications become connected.

For collection and qualification, incoming leads should follow a standardized intake process regardless of their source. Required fields should be validated, contact details normalized, and existing records checked before processing. AI can interpret enquiries and assign qualification categories, while fixed rules handle missing information, duplicates, and cases that need human review.

For synchronization, each lead should have a unique identifier and a traceable history of changes. This allows information to remain consistent across the CRM and other connected applications. Follow-up messages should be triggered by specific status changes and conditions, rather than every time a record is updated. That helps avoid duplicate notifications and unnecessary contact.

Reliability requires more than simply adding a retry node. The workflow should capture failed executions, distinguish temporary errors from permanent ones, apply appropriate retry limits, and alert someone when manual intervention is needed. Testing should include expired credentials, unavailable APIs, malformed data, rate limits, and interrupted executions.

Full disclosure: I’m associated with Pond AI, which builds, runs, and maintains custom AI agents and workflows. Pond AI can create a free architecture blueprint for you to keep and implement yourself or share with a freelancer. If you engage Pond AI for the actual build, there’s a 7 day refund policy.

Which integrations will the workflow depend on, and are there any APIs with rate limits or reliability issues that need special handling?

posts.name: Julis James
posts.cooked:
Hi Nurul, thanks for sharing your experience and proposed approach.

The goal is to consolidate leads from multiple sources into one central system. Validation and duplicate detection must happen before AI qualification to prevent the same contact from being processed more than once.

The CRM/database, AI provider, and follow-up channels are still open to the best technical recommendation. The expected daily lead volume is also yet to be finalized.

Your experience with lead scoring and follow-up automation is relevant. Could you share how you handled duplicate detection across multiple lead sources in your previous project, particularly when the same contact came through different channels?

posts.name: Julis James
posts.cooked:
You’ve raised some important points, particularly around scalability and execution reliability.

The integrations are not fixed yet. The priority is to connect multiple lead sources to a central CRM or database, with validation and duplicate checks completed before AI qualification. I’m open to recommendations on the most suitable CRM, AI provider, and follow-up channels.

There are no known API limitations at this point, but the design should account for rate limits, failed requests, and recovery.

Which integration stack would you recommend, and how would you prevent duplicate processing when multiple sources submit the same contact?

Thanks for clarifying. I’d recommend a centralized CRM with a standardized intake layer, normalized contact details, and database-level unique checks before qualification. For reliability, I’d also use controlled retries, rate-limit handling, and failed-execution alerts.

posts.cooked:
UPDATE: ENOUGH RESPONSES RECEIVED

Thank you to everyone who responded and shared their ideas. I’ve received enough applications and helpful suggestions to move forward, so I’m closing this post and won’t be considering additional responses for now.

To avoid the thread becoming overcrowded and burying other members’ questions and relevant discussions, please hold off on submitting further applications or sending additional messages about this opportunity.

I’ll review the responses already received and in the coming days, will reach out privately to the people whose experience best fits the project. I appreciate everyone who took the time to contribute and understand if I’m unable to respond to each person individually.

Thanks again for your understanding and support.

Hi Manisman,

Thank you for the clarification.

In my previous AI Lead Qualification project, I used Google Sheets as a central data source to check incoming leads against existing records before sending them to AI qualification.

If a matching record was found, the workflow marked the lead as a duplicate and stopped further processing. New leads continued to the AI scoring process.

For multiple channels, my proposed approach would be:

  1. Normalize contact information, such as email addresses and phone numbers, into a consistent format.

  2. Check these identifiers against a central database before AI qualification.

  3. If a matching contact is found, update the existing record and log the new source instead of creating another lead.

  4. If the match is uncertain, flag it for manual review.

  5. Use a unique lead identifier and processing status to help prevent duplicate actions during retries.

I have implemented basic duplicate detection in my previous project, while cross-channel matching is an area I would approach as an extension of that system.

I’d also like to understand which lead sources and CRM platforms you are considering.

Best regards,
Nurul

posts.name: Ben Ron
posts.cooked:
Hi Manisman, I’d lock down first what happens when a run stops halfway. I’d give each lead one ID at the form and check it before every CRM write or follow-up, so a retry can’t send a second message or create a second record.

Duplicates get matched on email and phone before the AI categorises anything. Thin submissions go to a review list. I’ve built a Finsure to HubSpot sync for a mortgage brokerage.

Which forms and CRM are involved, and roughly how many leads a day?
